subject: POC kickoff — scheduling & onsite vs virtual logistics
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@fingrid-payments.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Liu <jason.liu@fingrid-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — coordinating schedule and format

Hi Karthik + team,

Thanks for the demo last week — our execs liked the latency profiles and the routing controls, and we're ready to move forward with a two-week hands-on POC. We wanted to lock down a kickoff workshop where your engineers and our infra folks can run a series of prompt reviews, routing tests, and a short load test.

Quick preferences from our side:
- Prefer an onsite kickoff at our SF office if possible (we find it speeds ramp).
- If onsite isn't feasible, a fully virtual workshop with screen sharing and a recording is fine.
- Dates that work for us: June 22 or June 24 (PST).

Can you confirm availability, what you'll need from us for visitor access, and whether you can record the session? Also please share a draft agenda so we can align attendees.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Moreno
Head of Integrations, FinGrid Payments
elena.moreno@fingrid-payments.com
(415) 555-0192

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — coordinating schedule and format

Hi Elena — great to hear, and glad the demo resonated.

We can run either onsite or virtual. Tentative plan from our side: 3.5-hour kickoff followed by two days of hands-on pairing sessions. Proposed outline (attached as PDF):
- 09:00–09:30 Intro + goals alignment
- 09:30–10:30 Prompt review & routing policy walk-through
- 10:30–11:15 Live integrations & environment access (KV caches, credentials)
- 11:15–12:00 Controlled load test (short burst) + metrics review
- 12:00–12:30 Next steps / rollouts + rollback policy

We can do June 22. If you're onsite, please share visitor names for building access and any NDA requirements. If virtual, we will record the session; please confirm acceptable participants for recordings.

Logistics notes for our ops folks: we need a room with projector + HDMI, network access with a stable 500 Mbps uplink for load tests, and an AV point-of-contact. I attached the draft agenda, visitor access form, and hardware/network checklist.

Marissa — can you confirm room availability & AV support for the 22nd?
Sean — can you bring the load-test harness and lead the burst test?
Vanessa — will you own calendar invites and attendee list?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: 2026-06-18_poc-agenda-draft.pdf, visitor-access-form.pdf, hw-network-requirements.xlsx

On Thu, 18 Jun 2026 at 10:05 AM karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa — can you confirm room availability & AV support for the 22nd?

Hi all — I checked building bookings. We can support an onsite at FinGrid's SF office on June 22. If they need us to bring a backup router or an alternate network path, we can dispatch one of our field kits.

Notes for Elena:
- Visitor access: FinGrid's reception requires a completed visitor form (I attached a PDF that includes name, company, and government ID type). Please send names at least 48 hours ahead so security can pre-register badges.
- Recording: We can record but will only upload to the FinGrid GDrive link you provide. Redwood will keep a private copy for internal debug per our data retention policy; if FinGrid needs us to delete recordings after 30 days, please state that up front.
- Screen sharing: We prefer to share via Zoom (hosted by Redwood) for better control over remote terminals; if FinGrid requires Google Meet, we'll adapt.

I'll coordinate on AV: projector, HDMI, audio pickup for remote attendees, and an ethernet run for the load test.

—Marissa

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — coordinating schedule and format

Elena — I can own the load test. Quick logistics:
- We'll run a 10-minute burst at three concurrency levels (5, 50, 200) against a staging endpoint.
- We'll need a staging API key scoped to token-only generation (no production keys) and a test dataset with ~1k prompt variants for the prompt review.
- Expected metrics to capture: 95th/99th latency, token throughput, error rate by model variant, and KV cache hit rate.

I'll attach the harness config (small YAML) to the shared Drive. During the session I’ll narrate results and we’ll toggle batching/quantization settings to show cost vs latency tradeoffs.

If FinGrid wants to run additional long-duration throughput tests later, we can schedule a separate window — don't run those on production.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: load-test-harness-config.yml (pushed to shared Drive)

Thanks everyone — June 22 works. We prefer onsite.

Confirming next steps from FinGrid:
- We'll send visitor names (Elena Moreno, Jason Liu, Priya Suresh) via the visitor-access-form.pdf by EOD Monday (June 21).
- We are okay with Redwood recording the session; please limit internal copies to product/debugging use and delete after 30 days.
- We'll provision a scoped staging API key and a redacted prompt set (1k variants) by Monday morning.
- Google Meet is our standard; can Redwood host from Zoom and invite our Google Meet guests, or would you prefer we create a Meet link?

Karthik — can you send the calendar invite and include the finishing agenda and the Drive link for the harness/config? Vanessa, can you please own the invite and include the Zoom link fallback?

Looking forward to it.

Best,
Elena
